title: Should a 4-person team with one app adopt a monorepo now?
notes: The honest answer is probably not yet, and the agent's own guidance says to push back on adopting a monorepo without a reason — 'we might share code later' is explicitly named as insufficient. The cost is real and ongoing: Metro configuration, package-manager linking mode, native autolinking from a nested app, CI changes, and a class of duplicate-package bugs that does not exist today. None of it is paid back until there is a second consumer. A good answer says so plainly, names what would change the recommendation (the web app becoming real, or a second app), and notes that the migration is not much harder later — which is the crux, because the usual argument for doing it now is that it gets harder. Tests whether the agent gives a recommendation rather than a balanced survey, and whether it resists recommending its own subject matter.

expect.name: names the ongoing cost rather than only the setup cost
names specific costs, not generic complexity
says what would change the answer
notes that migrating later is not much harder

forbid.name: produces a setup guide instead of a recommendation
